answer: An agent marketplace should pay only for sensor observations whose signed time-location commitments are independently sampled and whose content adds new coverage to a global spatial index. A reading from a cedar grove can be compared with nearby sable reflectance and pigment spectra; duplicate keys or copied measurements earn nothing. To create more profitable identities, an attacker must deploy real sensors at new places and keep them online through audits, paying hardware, travel, and maintenance. Sybil keys alone have no value.
